name: Disorder of Cobalamin Metabolism and Transport

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Cobalamin Metabolism Disorders

criteria.description: Elevated methylmalonic acid levels in blood or urine
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in cobalamin metabolism or transport (e.g., MMACHC, MMADHC)
Presence of neurological and/or hematological abnormalities consistent with cobalamin deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated methylmalonic acid and homocysteine levels plus pathogenic genetic variant in cobalamin metabolism gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by clinical presentation and response to cobalamin supplementation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord
pathognomonic.notes: Demyelination affecting dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts
searchTerms: gradual loss of spinal cord function

pathognomonic.notes: Biochemical hallmark of cobalamin metabolic defects

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

common.symptomName: Gastrointestinal disturbances including diarrhea and vomiting
searchTerms: stomach upset with diarrhea and vomiting
digestive problems including loose stools and throwing up
GI symptoms like nausea and diarrhea

occasional.symptomName: Optic neuropathy leading to visual impairment
searchTerms: optic nerve damage causing vision loss
eye nerve problems leading to poor sight

occasional.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations including depression and irritability

laboratory: Elevated methylmalonic acid in plasma and urine
Low serum cobalamin levels (may be normal in transport defects)
imaging: MRI showing hyperintensity in dorsal columns of spinal cord
Brain MRI may show cerebral atrophy or white matter changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MMACHC, MMADHC, MUT, or other cobalamin metabolism genes
other: Abnormal cellular uptake of cobalamin in fibroblast studies

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated folate deficiency without methylmalonic acid elevation
Autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells
Primary enzymatic defect in methylmalonyl-CoA mutase

redFlags: Severe megaloblastic anemia refractory to folate supplementation
Early onset metabolic crisis with acidosis
references: Watkins D, Rosenblatt DS. Inherited disorders of cobalamin transport and metabolism. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2011.
Fowler B. Disorders of vitamin B12 metabolism. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2001.
Orphanet: Disorder of cobalamin metabolism and transport. ORPHA:79171.
